web.radiosettings.title: Radio settings
web.radiosettings.open.detail: Name, frequency, power and position of the radio this page is holding.
web.radiosettings.noRadio: There is no radio to set. Connect one over Bluetooth or USB first. The development bridge and the recorded data have no radio behind them.
web.radiosettings.deaf: Nothing heard since connecting. If the mesh is within reach of this radio, the four values under Radio are the first thing to check against it.
web.radiosettings.name.label: Name
web.radiosettings.name.foot: The name other radios see in this radio's adverts. The firmware keeps 31 bytes of it, so a name in an accented or non-Latin script fits fewer characters than a plain one.
web.radiosettings.radio.label: Radio
web.radiosettings.radio.foot: A radio hears only the radios that are on exactly these four values. One step out on any of them and it hears nothing at all, while still connecting, answering and naming itself here. Choosing a preset fills the fields in; nothing goes to the radio until Apply.
web.radiosettings.power.label: Transmit power
web.radiosettings.power.unknown: This radio has not said what its highest power is, so none can be set.
web.radiosettings.power.foot: More power carries further and drains the battery faster. The highest value offered is the one this radio reports it can do.
web.radiosettings.position.label: Position
web.radiosettings.position.locating: Asking this browser where it is.
web.radiosettings.position.refused: This browser gave no location. Allow it for this site, or type the two numbers.
web.radiosettings.position.foot: Where the radio says it is, to a millionth of a degree. An advert carries it only when the radio's advert location policy shares it, which the row above reports.
web.radiosettings.contacts.label: Contacts
web.radiosettings.contacts.autoAdd.detai: Off means a node the radio hears is not kept in its list until somebody adds it.
web.radiosettings.contacts.foot: This is the firmware's manual-add setting. Writing it sends back every other value in the same command exactly as the radio reported it.
web.radiosettings.advert.label: Advert
web.radiosettings.advert.foot: An advert tells the mesh this radio's name, key and, when the policy shares it, its position. Flood travels on through repeaters; zero hop is heard only by what is in direct range.
web.radiosettings.reboot.label: Restart
web.radiosettings.reboot.sent: The radio was told to restart.
web.radiosettings.reboot.foot: A restart is how some firmware settles a change it took but did not act on.
web.radiosettings.reboot.confirm.title: Restart %@?
web.radiosettings.reboot.confirm.message: The radio restarts and this page loses it. A radio this browser has already been given is picked up again once it is back. Anything the radio was holding for this page stays on the radio.
web.radiosettings.invalid.frequency: The frequency has to be a number between %1$@ and %2$@ MHz.
web.radiosettings.invalid.bandwidth: The bandwidth has to be a number between %1$@ and %2$@ kHz.
web.radiosettings.invalid.spreadingFacto: The spreading factor has to be a whole number between %1$@ and %2$@.
web.radiosettings.invalid.codingRate: The coding rate has to be a whole number between %1$@ and %2$@.
web.radiosettings.invalid.latitude: The latitude has to be a number between %1$@ and %2$@.
web.radiosettings.invalid.longitude: The longitude has to be a number between %1$@ and %2$@.
web.radiosettings.invalid.other: That value is not one the radio takes.
web.radiosettings.error.notConnected: The radio is no longer connected.
web.radiosettings.error.illegalArgument: The radio refused that value and stayed as it was.
web.radiosettings.error.unsupported: This radio's firmware does not have that command.
web.radiosettings.error.badState: The radio would not do that just now.
